messages.content: You are an experienced power-plant performance engineer. Answer with a single JSON object and nothing else.

A combined cycle power plant has one gas turbine, a heat recovery steam generator and a steam turbine. It runs at full load. Hourly records give net electrical output (MW) together with ambient temperature (2 to 37 degC), ambient pressure, relative humidity and condenser vacuum. The plant has no inlet cooling, and over this ambient range the gas turbine stays below the rated limit of its generator. On cold, humid days an inlet anti-icing system heats the intake air with compressor bleed.

Question: over the 2 to 37 degC ambient range, is there a temperature beyond which the net output responds to ambient temperature differently from elsewhere (much more weakly, or in the opposite direction)? There may be none, one or more on the cold side, one on the hot side, or several.
Reply with JSON only, in this form:
{"boundaries": [{"side": "below" or "above", "at_c": <degC>, "rh_above": <percent, or null>, "mechanism": "power_cap" or "anti_icing" or "evap_cooling" or "other", "output_trend": "rises" or "falls" or "about the same", "confidence": <0 to 1>}], "rationale": "<one or two sentences>"}
"side": "below" means the different response holds below at_c; "above" means above at_c. "rh_above" is the relative humidity above which it applies, or null if it applies at any humidity. "mechanism" names the cause: power_cap is a generator or power limit, anti_icing is inlet anti-icing heating, evap_cooling is inlet evaporative cooling. "output_trend" says how net output changes as ambient temperature moves further beyond at_c. Use an empty list if you expect no such temperature.

response: {"boundaries": [{"side": "below", "at_c": 2, "rh_above": 80, "mechanism": "anti_icing", "output_trend": "falls", "confidence": 0.8}], "rationale": "The anti-icing system activates on cold, humid days, reducing net output, and this effect becomes more pronounced as temperature drops further below 2 degC. The impact is most significant at higher relative humidities, above 80%."}

Hourly records give net electrical output (MW) together with ambient temperature (2 to 37 degC), ambient pressure, relative humidity and condenser vacuum. The plant has no inlet cooling, and over this ambient range the gas turbine stays below the rated limit of its generator. On cold, humid days an inlet anti-icing system heats the intake air with compressor bleed.
Training data available: 146 hourly records with ambient temperature between 19.1 and 21.6 degC. Within these records a linear fit gives d(output)/d(temperature) = -3.65 MW/degC (standard error 0.55). Predictions are needed outside this temperature range.

Question: over the 2 to 37 degC ambient range, is there a temperature beyond which the net output responds to ambient temperature differently from elsewhere (much more weakly, or in the opposite direction)? There may be none, one or more on the cold side, one on the hot side, or several.
Reply with JSON only, in this form:
{"boundaries": [{"side": "below" or "above", "at_c": <degC>, "rh_above": <percent, or null>, "mechanism": "power_cap" or "anti_icing" or "evap_cooling" or "other", "output_trend": "rises" or "falls" or "about the same", "confidence": <0 to 1>}], "rationale": "<one or two sentences>"}
"side": "below" means the different response holds below at_c; "above" means above at_c. "rh_above" is the relative humidity above which it applies, or null if it applies at any humidity. "mechanism" names the cause: power_cap is a generator or power limit, anti_icing is inlet anti-icing heating, evap_cooling is inlet evaporative cooling. "output_trend" says how net output changes as ambient temperature moves further beyond at_c. Use an empty list if you expect no such temperature.

response: {"boundaries": [{"side": "below", "at_c": 19.1, "rh_above": 100, "mechanism": "anti_icing", "output_trend": "falls", "confidence": 0.7}], "rationale": "The anti-icing system is expected to activate on cold and humid days, altering the net output response to ambient temperature, and there is no indication of a change in response on the hot side within the given range."}

Hourly records give net electrical output (MW) together with ambient temperature (2 to 37 degC), ambient pressure, relative humidity and condenser vacuum. The plant has no inlet cooling. In cold weather the gas turbine reaches the rated limit of its generator, and the control system holds it at that limit. On cold, humid days an inlet anti-icing system heats the intake air with compressor bleed. At 15 degC and 1013 mbar the gas turbine alone produces about 343 MW. The gas turbine generator is limited to 364 MW. Anti-icing keeps the compressor inlet at about 7 degC when relative humidity is above about 70%.
Training data available: 146 hourly records with ambient temperature between 31.3 and 33.8 degC. Within these records a linear fit gives d(output)/d(temperature) = -2.38 MW/degC (standard error 0.67). Predictions are needed outside this temperature range.

Question: over the 2 to 37 degC ambient range, is there a temperature beyond which the net output responds to ambient temperature differently from elsewhere (much more weakly, or in the opposite direction)? There may be none, one or more on the cold side, one on the hot side, or several.
Reply with JSON only, in this form:
{"boundaries": [{"side": "below" or "above", "at_c": <degC>, "rh_above": <percent, or null>, "mechanism": "power_cap" or "anti_icing" or "evap_cooling" or "other", "output_trend": "rises" or "falls" or "about the same", "confidence": <0 to 1>}], "rationale": "<one or two sentences>"}
"side": "below" means the different response holds below at_c; "above" means above at_c. "rh_above" is the relative humidity above which it applies, or null if it applies at any humidity. "mechanism" names the cause: power_cap is a generator or power limit, anti_icing is inlet anti-icing heating, evap_cooling is inlet evaporative cooling. "output_trend" says how net output changes as ambient temperature moves further beyond at_c. Use an empty list if you expect no such temperature.

response: {"boundaries": [{"side": "below", "at_c": 15, "rh_above": 70, "mechanism": "anti_icing", "output_trend": "about the same", "confidence": 0.8}, {"side": "below", "at_c": 7, "rh_above": null, "mechanism": "power_cap", "output_trend": "about the same", "confidence": 0.9}], "rationale": "The anti-icing system and power cap introduce temperature boundaries beyond which the net output responds differently to ambient temperature, with the power cap being more confident due to the direct limit on generator output."}
